h1: Laser cutting machines for sheet and plate — enclosed, open-type, plate and sheet-and-tube lasers, 1.5 to 80 kW
intro: A fiber laser cutting machine cuts sheet and plate from a DXF file with a focused beam — mild steel to 1-1/2″ and beyond with the high-power sources, stainless and aluminum to 1″ — at speeds no plasma or punch can match, with a clean edge and no tooling. NovoTech sells five kinds in Canada, each on its own page: enclosed lasers with a laser-safe cabin and an exchange table or pallet changer, the production machine from 4 × 4 ft compact models to 8.5 × 41 ft and 80 kW; open-type single-table and semi-closed lasers, the entry and long-plate machines to 85 ft; large-format plate lasers on ground rails or gantries to 10 × 164 ft with bevel heads; sheet-and-tube combination lasers with a rotary chuck beside the table; and 3D laser cells and coil-fed lines. Each kind comes in a premium line made in Turkey and a value line built to our specification, as sections on the same page. Below, the five kinds compared, the laser power guide and every model in one table of working area, power and speed; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller, nesting software, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Enclosed, open-type, plate or sheet-and-tube — which laser should I buy?
faq.a: By how many sheets a day and what they are. An enclosed laser with an exchange table or pallet changer keeps cutting while you load the next sheet and keeps fumes and the beam inside — the production machine, and the one most shops buy from 5 × 10 ft up. An open-type single-table laser stops while you load but costs less and takes sheets from any side — the first laser, and the only kind for 20 to 85 ft plate on a single table. A ground-rail or gantry plate laser is for heavy plate and very long beds, with bevel heads and oxy-fuel. A sheet-and-tube laser adds a rotary chuck beside the table for a shop that cuts both and has room for one machine. 3D cells cut formed parts; coil-fed lines cut straight from the coil. Each kind has its own page with the premium and value lines side by side.

The premium Dener lasers are built in Turkey on frames rated for 1.5 G, with Precitec heads, IPG / nLIGHT sources, the longest life at high duty and Dener Canada parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada — for two shifts a day. NovoTech's own value line and the Senfeng value line are built in China with their own or Raycus sources, in a wider range — 4 × 4 ft compact machines, 60 – 80 kW plate gantries, sheet-and-tube combos, coil-fed lines — at a lower price; NovoTech stocks the parts and does the service for all of them. Same cut quality at the same power; the premium machine is faster between parts and lasts longer at high duty.

faq.q: What laser power do I need?
faq.a: Power sets the thickness and the speed. As a guide for mild steel: 3 kW cuts 1/2″, 6 kW 3/4″ (and 1/4″ at over 300 in/min), 12 kW 1″, 20 kW 1-1/4″ and 30 – 40 kW 1-1/2″ and beyond; stainless and aluminum run about 20 – 30 % thinner at the same power, with nitrogen or air assist. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW: thick enough for structural work, fast enough to pay for the machine on thin sheet. Tell us your material mix and we run the cutting chart for you.

The model number is the nominal working area in centimetres: 3015 = 10 × 5 ft (3,000 × 1,500 mm) — a standard 4 × 8 or 5 × 10 sheet; 4020 = 13 × 6.6 ft; 6020 = 20 × 6.6 ft for 6 × 20 plate; 6025 and 8025 = 20 and 26 ft × 8.2 ft; 12526 = 41 × 8.5 ft. The 5 × 10 machine is the Canadian standard; buy the 6020 if you cut 20 ft plate or want to nest several sheets without reloading; the 4 × 4 ft Senfeng compact is for small parts in a small shop.

faq.q: Single table, double table or pallet changer?
faq.a: A single-table machine (Dener Smart open and semi-closed, NovoTech ULF, Senfeng compact and NP) stops while you unload and load — fine for a few sheets an hour and the lowest price. A double table or pallet changer (Dener GFL and Smart closed, NovoTech ULE, Senfeng H series) swaps tables in 15 to 20 seconds, so the laser cuts while the operator loads: the difference between 40 and 70 % spindle time on a busy machine, and the base for a loading tower later.

faq.q: What about assist gas and fume extraction?
faq.a: Oxygen gives the fastest cut and an oxide edge on mild steel; nitrogen a clean, paint-ready edge on all metals; compressed air at 16 bar replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″ and cuts the gas bill to near zero — the intelligent air-cutting package is an option on both lines. The machines have pneumatic extraction compartments under the table and connect to a dust collector, which we can supply.

Yes — a loading / unloading tower that feeds the pallet changer, sheet storage with several shelves for lights-out production, part sorting, and bevel heads for weld preparation. The Dener GFL and closed-type Smart, the NovoTech ULE and the Senfeng H series are prepared for the tower; the Senfeng coil-fed lines go further and cut straight from the coil. Ask us for the automation layout.

faq.q: What does the machine need on site?
faq.a: A level floor, 600 V 3-phase (with the transformer we supply) or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas, a dust collector and a compressed-air supply for air cutting. A 6 kW 3015 draws about 30 kW in total and needs roughly 33 × 20 ft with a pallet changer. Delivery, installation and operator training are done by NovoTech from Mississauga, ON, Canada, and the Ontario pre-start health and safety review is prepared by us.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
